static_projection.method: Replace the 24 baseline #[cfg(all(cw32l010, rcc_lse))] predicates with #[cfg(rcc_lse)]; remove the one candidate L011-only UART3 cfg-and-tuple pair; remove only whole line comments beginning with optional spaces and // from both files; compare remaining UTF-8 bytes.
static_projection.interpretation: Source selection for existing qualified L010 is equivalent; actual compiler/linker regression is not established by this projection.

criteria.finding: The shared backend is selected only for native L010/L011 register versions. Existing generated rcc_lse remains an exact-package auxiliary gate, and the new detector-presence assertions separately add only CW32L011K8T6/K8U6. L012 remains on its unchanged backend.

Missing Lse, invalid declaration/budget/conditions and bus overspeed fail before RCC mutation. Declared LSE bounds propagate by cumulative divisors; configured HSI is checked separately; full own fixed-fallback bound has no AHB/APB divider credit.

The first-request boolean uses original entry LSI.STABLE with needs_trim || needs_lsi. It is consumed once after retained-owner inspection and again immediately before LSIEN. No intervening STABLE transition reclassifies that boolean.

The added L011-only UART3 tuple uses the same central RccInfo inspection path as UART1/2. Own APBEN1 offset 56 bit 8 is configuration-only, keyed 0x5A5A and active-high; APBRST1 offset 72 bit 8 is active-low. SOURCE bits13:12 bind typed LSI encoding 3 in both production metadata validation layers.

Each UART checks held reset before inspection, in the SOURCE read closure and after restoration. SOURCE = 3 rejects independently of RXEN/TXEN. inspect_for_init restores the exact incoming gate after a read and attempts restoration even after enable failure. The restoration error is propagated before the saved semantic conflict is interpreted.
The target maps EnableFailed and RestoreFailed to distinct enable_failed/restore_failed fields. Non-LSE HSI/HSE and auxiliary-only calls retain their prior generic retained-inspection classification.

RTC SOURCE = 2/reserved, enabled LPTIM LSI, MCO4, LSIRDY and enabled LSI-filtered VC/LVD including zero filter count remain vetoes. No timer work gate or uninspected observer is opened to infer idleness. Whole-bank GPIO, timer LSI_OUT, IWDT and downstream/external progress remain explicit functional handovers.

The ordinary legal cold path retains factory-HSI read/mask, guarded HSI to unchanged LSI to factory HSI calibration, conditional CLKCCS suspension/restoration, unchanged LSI TRIM/WAIT and restoration of only the original software LSIEN request. StartupOnly gains no factory-LSI condition.

The unchanged native preflight admits monitored L011 only with initially stable, non-erased own factory-matching ten-bit LSI at 0x001007C2. The target preserves original entry readiness and parameters around refresh. Later bridge readiness cannot create initial monitor admission. The 41000 Hz detector envelope remains distinct from the RM legal-adjustment prerequisite.

RTC SOURCE = 3 still requires already factory-ready raw HSIOSC for an oscillator-changing transition. MCO3 and HSIRDY guard necessary HSI start/restart/unready entry. A live divider-only update preserves raw HSIOSC; public documentation explicitly covers PB0 AF3 raw-HSI observers. Existing HSIOSC calendar capability remains unchanged.

WAIT3 is obtained from own generated constants, raised and read back before guarded transitions. Before and after native admission refresh, only the typed FLASHWAIT alias is normalized; original non-WAIT CR2, IER, MCO, LSE and LSI parameters remain bound.

Native low-power leaf bytes are unchanged. Own GPIOC PC14/PC15, PINLOCK/LSELOCK, drives, exact reuse, RTC quiet-image admission, LPTIM trigger 1–4 distinction, monitors and preserved IRQ/brake routes remain native. Final pad inspection is followed by target verification.

The target installs and verifies final AHB/APB divisors under calibrated HSI, then performs its last CR0 write selecting LSE. The remaining target tail only reads CR0, so a subsequent divider read-modify-write cannot overwrite fallback with LSE.

Final WAIT covers declared LSE upper HCLK, configured factory-HSI upper HCLK and full 4.08 MHz fallback using the own 24 MHz step. Fault, source, policy, monitor, mux, divisor and authoritative WAIT checks continue after final GPIOC verification. Only configure success reaches the single CLOCKS publication point.

The exact approved public-init insertion is the only lib.rs change and its removal reproduces baseline bytes. It describes the legal/factory distinction, UART3 and both first-request passes, raw-HSI observer, native pad rules, fixed fallback, failure/reset limits and rejected 1 MHz time driver.

After normalizing exactly 24 old cfg predicates and removing exactly the L011-only UART3 tuple, the comment-stripped shared source is identical. Qualified L010 sees equivalent predicates and excludes UART3. Qualified L011 non-LSE calls keep lse_target=None and all new target checks inactive. All 15 other recursive RCC Rust files match baseline. This is static evidence, not build or execution evidence.

resolved_findings.finding: Initial proof additions used 60/76. Final receipt and both production assertion layers now use the own APBEN1 offset 56 and APBRST1 offset 72, bit 8; the runtime always used the correct central RccInfo.
The final production checks bind the actual selected UART3 SOURCE enum variant LSI=3, in addition to field offset/width and the qualification scalar.

limits.build_and_elf_correspondence: Pending separate inspection of actual completed build logs, generated outputs and linked ELF identities. This source review does not claim that any build or regression has passed.
limits.electrical_scope: No measurement of legal trim, clock rate, jitter, board conditions, Flash alias timing, fallback register mutation or fault survival. Factory monitor envelope and RM legal-entry conditions remain separate.
limits.freeze_scope: Acceptance applies only to the listed hashes. A later change to reviewed runtime, public contract, metadata bindings or generated register identities requires re-review.
